sources: Built from 25 web searches and 27 page fetches · Baltimore Ravens official injury report, NFL.com, AtlantaFalcons.com, Giants.com, Panthers.com, Commanders.com, Sharp Football Analysis, FantasyPros, Pro Football Network, DraftKings Network, Sports Illustrated/OnSI, NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, Bleacher Nation, Bleacher Report, ESPN

tonight.headline: Still 40.8–0, and the tight-end card this brief opened at 04:40 is still sitting unfired.
body: Nothing has moved on the scoreboard since Thursday. Josh Allen's 40.8 is the only score either side has, and Panda Attack's Dalton Kincaid already banked 22.5 for them — on their bench, where it does not count. Eleven of your fourteen play Sunday morning.

There is exactly one thing to do before 11:00 tomorrow: drop Kyle Pitts and add Mark Andrews. That was true at 04:40 this morning, it is still true now, and Andrews is still a free agent. Everything else on this roster is correctly set.

case.label: Where the 59% comes from
case.body: ESPN has AVIATO 143.5 to 125.1 on live projections. That gap is mostly Allen: he beat his 22.9 projection by 17.9 on Thursday and no one on Panda Attack can bank a Thursday score any more — Kincaid's 22.5 came off their bench.

case.label: The script that beats you
case.body: Panda Attack start Dak Prescott, George Pickens and Harrison Mevis in the Dallas–Washington 20:25 window, plus Javonte Williams in the RB/WR flex. That is four starters in one game. A Dallas shootout is the single script that turns 143–125 around, and your own Terry McLaurin is on the other side of it.

case.label: What you can do about it
case.body: About the scoreboard, nothing — your lineup is locked in shape and correct. About next week, one thing: the Pitts seat. That is the card below.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Jordan Mason is on Panda Attack's bench at INJURY_RESERVE and Dalton Kincaid has already played. If they add a live body before Sunday 11:00 the 125.1 moves, but not by enough to matter without Dallas going off.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Both games kick off Sunday 11:00 Mexico City
doFirst.title: Drop Kyle Pitts, add Mark Andrews
doFirst.subtitle: Same card as this morning, re-checked against a 21:52 snapshot and still unfired. Andrews is a free agent — no waiver priority, no claim, just add.

case.label: The seat, not the player
case.body: Chem's flex is RB/WR only. A second tight end cannot enter your lineup in any week this season unless Isaiah Likely is out. So this seat is worth exactly what its occupant is worth on the one Sunday Likely misses — and today it is occupied by a man catching passes from a third-string quarterback.

case.label: Who is throwing to Pitts
case.body: Cooper Rush. NFL.com and AtlantaFalcons.com both named him the Week 2 starter with Michael Penix Jr. ruled out again. This is the exact failure the brief logged once before — Pitts projected 9.8 and scored 0.0 behind Atlanta's third quarterback — and it is the same quarterback room.

case.label: Who is throwing to Andrews
case.body: Lamar Jackson, into a receiver room that has run out of people. Zay Flowers is DOUBTFUL on Baltimore's own Friday report with a hamstring (ESPN's file has already moved him to OUT), Ja'Kobi Lane is out, and Sports Illustrated's must-start column expects Andrews to see double-digit targets because 'the Ravens are out of options.' He went 4 for 49 in Week 1 with Flowers healthy.

case.label: Dropping a 93% player, on the record
case.body: Pitts is rostered in 93.3% of leagues and this brief is telling you to cut him, which needs a reason that disagrees with the market. It is this: the market prices him as a startable TE1, and in a RB/WR flex he is not startable at all. Yesterday's exhaustive pair search across all nine other Chem rosters found no team that would give anything for him, and that search re-ran clean tonight. He is a 93%-owned player with no lineup slot and no trade market.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Zay Flowers appears ACTIVE on Baltimore's Sunday inactive list, which puts Andrews back behind a healthy WR1 and makes this a hold. Or Isaiah Likely turns up on a Giants report before Monday night — he is not on the one published for the Rams game — which would make Pitts the only tight end you own.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only — do not fire this today
doFirst.title: Kyle Monangai for Jaylen Warren at RB2 — still do not fire this
doFirst.subtitle: Published unarmed this morning on a snap count. Tonight's reporting cuts against it, and the card is downgraded rather than deleted.

case.label: Why it exists
case.body: This brief graded Warren on carries for two consecutive runs and never reported that Rico Dowdle out-snapped him 57.8% to 35.9% and out-routed him 48.8% to 30.2% in Week 1. The ghost card was the honest way to put that on the screen without churning a starting slot on it.

case.label: What tonight changed
case.body: Two sources now disagree about the size of that gap. FantasyPros' Week 2 Primer keeps the snap split and still calls Warren a possible RB2 against a New England run defence it grades permissive. Sports Illustrated's depth-chart column has them near level — Warren RB24, Dowdle RB27, both around a 45% run share, with Warren ahead on receiving work at 7% to 5%. I take Sports Illustrated's side on the split and FantasyPros' side on the matchup: the Week 1 snap gap was game script, and New England is the soft draw either way.

case.label: Why it stays unarmed
case.body: Warren is the one with the passing-down role, and in full PPR that is the half of the job that pays. Monangai is a Chicago back facing Minnesota with a quarterback change on the other sideline and no researched matchup grade. Swapping a 11.4 for a 9.9 to chase a snap count is the exact churn STRATEGY section 3 exists to stop.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Dowdle out-touches Warren again on Sunday at New England. Two straight weeks of that is a role, not a script, and the RB2 slot opens on Tuesday 22 September when the churn window expires. Conversely Warren clearing five targets closes this card for good.

doFirst.sources: FantasyPros Week 2 Primer · Sports Illustrated/OnSI · ESPN

whatWentWrong.title: Your bench tight end is behind a third-string quarterback, and has been all week
whatWentWrong.lead: Penix was ruled out again on Friday and Cooper Rush was named the starter. Pitts is still on your bench and the card telling you to cut him is twelve hours old.

case.label: The cost so far
case.body: None yet — Pitts is on your bench, so his Sunday cannot hurt your score. The cost is the seat: a roster spot on a 93%-owned player who cannot enter a RB/WR flex, held through a week when Mark Andrews became free.

case.label: Why it keeps happening
case.body: This brief has now named three different incoming players for this one seat — Mack Hollins over three runs, Rashod Bateman for one, now Andrews — and each was researched only after being named. Andrews is the first one where the reporting came first.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Firing the card. If Andrews is claimed by another Chem manager before 11:00 Sunday, the seat question reopens and the answer is no longer obvious — T.J. Hockenson and Hunter Henry are both free here, and neither can enter your flex either.

whatWentWrong.title: This brief told you Warren's role collapsed, then found the column that says it did not
whatWentWrong.lead: The 13:30 run put a ghost card on a 57.8-to-35.9 snap gap. Sports Illustrated has the two backs at a near-even run share with Warren ahead on receiving.

case.label: What was actually reported
case.body: FantasyPros: Dowdle 57.8% of snaps and 48.8% of routes, Warren 35.9% and 30.2%. Sports Illustrated, same week: Warren RB24 and Dowdle RB27, 'both around 45%' run share, receiving share 7% against 5% to Warren.

case.label: Why it matters to the card above
case.body: It is the reason the Monangai swap stays a ghost instead of being fired or deleted. One snapshot of snap counts in a game Pittsburgh led is not a role change, and Chem pays a point a reception.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Sunday's touch split at New England. If Dowdle repeats the Week 1 share, the SI read is wrong and the RB2 slot is live on Tuesday.

roster.footnote: One game is played and thirteen are not, so the right column is the matchup. Two tiles are dashed — Kyle Pitts (Carolina vs tight ends) and Kyle Monangai (Minnesota vs backs) — and that means I looked and found nothing published two games into the season, not that the matchup is average.

starting.name: Josh Allen
starting.detail: BUF · vs DET · FINAL · 40.8, which is 17.9 above his 22.9 pregame projection and the only score in this matchup. Nothing to do.

starting.name: De'Von Achane
starting.detail: MIA · at SF · SUN 14:25 · Malik Willis under centre — Miami cut Tyreek Hill and traded Jaylen Waddle, so Achane is the passing game. Miami carry the lowest implied total of any team you start. You start him anyway: in full PPR a heavy underdog's receiving back is the one role a losing script does not punish.
starting.gradeEvidence: SF 19th in rush yards allowed but a Tier-1 D/ST play vs MIA

starting.name: Jaylen Warren
starting.detail: PIT · at NE · SUN 11:00 · bad news on your own player, restated: Rico Dowdle led this backfield in Week 1 at 57.8% snaps and 48.8% routes to Warren's 35.9% and 30.2%, and took the only red-zone carry. Warren won the touches 15 to 10, and Sports Illustrated tonight have them near level — Warren RB24, Dowdle RB27, both around a 45% run share, Warren ahead on receiving 7% to 5%. He starts.

starting.name: Terry McLaurin
starting.detail: WSH · at DAL · SUN 14:25 · Jayden Daniels, absent from Washington's final report for a third straight day. The honest number: two catches for 14 yards in Week 1 on a 92.1% route share, while Diggs went 4 for 55 and a score and rookie Antonio Williams 4 for 64 and a score on 26 snaps. Daniels this week: 'not gonna force-feed Terry the ball.'
starting.gradeEvidence: DAL last in 3rd-down defence; Malik Hooker out, fractured forearm

starting.name: Justin Jefferson
starting.detail: MIN · at CHI · SUN 11:00 · Carson Wentz — Kyler Murray ruled out with a concussion. This is the rare quarterback change that helps: Wentz took 23 of Minnesota's 30 Week 1 dropbacks, so Jefferson's receiving-yard share was earned with Wentz throwing, and Sports Illustrated move him UP to WR6. Jordan Addison stays WR60 on the same news.

starting.name: Garrett Wilson
starting.detail: NYJ · vs GB · SUN 11:00 · Geno Smith, 19 of 24 in the opener · Wilson caught 6 of 7. Green Bay are without Micah Parsons until next month, which is the pass rush that would have decided this.
starting.gradeEvidence: SI list Green Bay as a Week 2 streaming D/ST (11% rostered)

starting.name: Isaiah Likely
starting.detail: NYG · at LAR · MON 18:15 · Jaxson Dart, QB4 in Week 1 · his thesis held again tonight: 8 of 8 for 78 and two touchdowns, targeted on 34.8% of his routes (TE3) and first among all tight ends in third-down target share at 57.1%. Route participation 67.6%, above the 60% floor his clause is written against — but that is TE20, and Malik Nabers took 9 targets on a 70.6% route rate beside him.
starting.gradeEvidence: Rams allowed the 6th-highest passing success rate in Wk 1; NYG implied 20.75

starting.name: Ravens D/ST
starting.detail: BAL · vs NO · SUN 11:00 · New Orleans start Tyler Shough. The comparison against the best available is in Do not chase and the answer is hold for a fifth consecutive run.
starting.gradeEvidence: SI Week 2 Start 'Em; Yahoo Tier 2 of 5

starting.name: Tyler Loop
starting.detail: BAL · vs NO · SUN 11:00 · Baltimore's implied total is the highest of any team on your roster and well clear of the 22-point floor his hold thesis is written against. Two sources disagree about him and the Do not chase row says which one I took.
starting.gradeEvidence: PFN Week 2 board: Loop K4 of 32

bench.name: Bhayshul Tuten
bench.detail: JAX · at DEN · SUN 14:05 · the best bench matchup you have · 48.2% snaps, a 46.9% designed-carry share and 33.3% routes in Week 1, and FantasyPros call him a must-start. He does not displace Warren at 11.4 to 10.1, and the RB2 slot is inside the churn window.
bench.gradeEvidence: Denver graded worse vs the run than the pass in Week 1

bench.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
bench.detail: ATL · vs CAR · SUN 11:00 · Cooper Rush, third string, with Penix ruled out again Friday and Tua out. He is the outgoing half of the card above. I did not research Carolina against tight ends, which is why this tile is dashed — but the quarterback, not the defence, is what makes this seat dead.

bench.name: Kyle Monangai
bench.detail: CHI · vs MIN · SUN 11:00 · Caleb Williams · off Chicago's injury report along with D'Andre Swift, who remains the lead back on snaps and carries. I did not research Minnesota's run defence this run, so the tile is dashed.

McLaurin keeps the flex on route share and because that slot is inside the churn window.
bench.gradeEvidence: Atlanta allowed 221 receiving yards on 37 targets in Week 1

worthALook.name: Jakobi Meyers
worthALook.lead: Still the biggest ownership anomaly on this board, and tonight's reporting says Sunday is the wrong week to find out.

case.label: Why he is here at all
case.body: 182.4 season projection, the highest of any receiver on the Chem wire, rostered in 76.8% of leagues nationally and a free agent here. STRATEGY section 4 calls widely-rostered-elsewhere-and-free-here the strongest single wire signal in a shallow league.

case.label: The number that argues against Sunday
case.body: He ran an 8.7% target share in Week 1 and finished WR28. He is at Denver, where FantasyPros note the Broncos allowed the second-fewest yards per target and the fewest fantasy points per target to perimeter receivers last season.

case.label: The thumb
case.body: NBC reported Thursday that Meyers (thumb) will play. That closes the availability question and leaves only the role question.

case.label: When to act
case.body: If Meyers out-targets Brian Thomas Jr. at Denver on Sunday while Thomas is shadowed by Patrick Surtain II, the move on Tuesday 22 September is Meyers in for Thomas — because that is Thomas's own thesis breaking, not a new discovery. If Thomas wins the split, Meyers comes off this list.

worthALook.sources: FantasyPros Week 2 Primer · NBC Sports · ESPN

worthALook.name: Khalil Shakir
worthALook.lead: On waivers here until Wednesday, which is after his game — so there is nothing to do about him this week and that is the whole point of the row.

case.label: The timing, which is the story
case.body: His clearsAt is 07:00Z on 23 September. Buffalo already played on Thursday. Whatever he did against Detroit is spent before you could ever have claimed him, so the sleeper note that surfaced him last week is irrelevant to Week 2.

case.label: Why he stays on the list anyway
case.body: 68.8% rostered nationally and free-to-claim here, and Chem priority resets weekly so a claim costs nothing lasting. AVIATO sits waiverRank 10, which means last in the queue this week — but the reset makes that a one-week cost, not a season one.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Wednesday 23 September, if his Thursday line showed six or more targets. The drop would be whichever bench body is worst after the Pitts seat resolves. Under six targets and he comes off the list.

doNotChase.name: Rashod Bateman
doNotChase.lead: The biggest single-day ownership move on this entire board, and the reporting says the people moving are wrong.

case.label: Why everyone is adding him
case.body: Zay Flowers is doubtful with a hamstring and Ja'Kobi Lane is out. Bateman is the name most managers reach for when a Ravens receiver room empties out, and his ownership moved +5.31 in a day off a 16.6% base.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: In Week 1, with Flowers healthy, Bateman ran a 4.2% target share — last among ten Ravens receivers — on one target, no catches and zero air yards. DraftKings Network's verdict for Week 2 is explicit: 'If Flowers is ruled out, Bateman is a Sit in all but the deepest formats.'

case.label: Where the targets actually go
case.body: Mark Andrews. Baltimore threw 25 times against 37 runs in Week 1, and vacated targets from a run-first offence concentrate on the tight end, not on the fifth receiver. That is the whole argument for the card at the top of this brief.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Bateman clearing seven targets on Sunday against New Orleans. That would say the Ravens do redistribute outside rather than inside, and it would also weaken the Andrews case by the same amount.

doNotChase.sources: DraftKings Network · Baltimore Ravens official injury report · Sports Illustrated/OnSI

doNotChase.name: Jordan Addison
doNotChase.lead: A 74.9%-owned receiver sitting free in your league looks like the anomaly you are told to buy. This one is priced correctly.

case.label: Why he looks free money
case.body: 171.4 season projection, rostered in three of every four leagues, free agent here, and he was dropped inside this league on 16 September. The why=OWNED band is exactly the signal STRATEGY tells you to respect.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Kyler Murray is out with a concussion and Carson Wentz starts. Sports Illustrated's fallout piece moves Justin Jefferson up to WR6 and leaves Addison at WR60, with the reason stated plainly: 'I do not believe that Wentz can support two viable wide receivers.' Wentz's own Week 2 projection is 183 passing yards.

case.label: The one you already own
case.body: The same quarterback change is why Jefferson's tile is dashed rather than green. You hold the receiver who survives a Wentz offence. Adding the one who does not is paying for the same news twice.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Wentz clearing 250 yards with Addison above a 20% target share, or Kyler Murray clearing concussion protocol for Week 3. Either reopens him, and Chem priority resets weekly so he would be cheap to claim then.

doNotChase.sources: Sports Illustrated/OnSI · NBC Sports · Bleacher Nation

doNotChase.name: Rachaad White
doNotChase.lead: Top why=OWNED running back on the board for a second straight run, declined for a second straight run, and the reason has not changed.

case.label: The role
case.body: RotoWire on his Commanders debut: 27 offensive snaps in a committee, with Jacory Croskey-Merritt taking the work that matters. He is the middle of a three-man backfield, which in full PPR is the worst shape a back can have — he collects the least valuable touches available.

case.label: Why the ownership number lies here
case.body: 66.1% is a draft-capital number, not a role number, and it is falling (−0.43 on the day). The band that matters is rising ownership on a vacated role. This is the opposite: static ownership on a shrinking one.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Croskey-Merritt missing a game, or White clearing five targets in a week. Either turns a committee body into a role. Logged so the next run does not rediscover him as a find.

doNotChase.name: Chase McLaughlin
doNotChase.lead: The weekly kicker comparison, answered hold for an eighth straight run. Tyler Loop is the best kicker available to you and it is not close.

case.label: The board
case.body: Pro Football Network's Week 2 kicker rankings: Tyler Loop K4. The best alternatives actually on the Chem wire are Chase McLaughlin K6, Tyler Bass K8, Eddy Pineiro K12 (and questionable), Trey Smack K13, Cairo Santos K14, Evan McPherson K15, Chris Boswell K17, Nick Folk K27.

case.label: Why Loop is K4
case.body: PFN: 'Baltimore's offence also gave him exactly the type of environment fantasy managers want from a kicker.' Baltimore host New Orleans, who are starting Tyler Shough. There is no kicker on this wire attached to a better scoring environment.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Loop finishing outside the top twenty in Week 2, or Baltimore's implied team total falling below 22 for two straight weeks. Then the seat opens on Tuesday and the answer is whoever tops the board that week.

doNotChase.name: Patriots D/ST
doNotChase.lead: The weekly defence comparison. Hold Baltimore — and note that the alternative this brief named last night has already been taken.

case.label: What changed today
case.body: Bok-aneers added the 49ers D/ST at 20:13 tonight and dropped Blake Corum to do it. San Francisco was the named fallback in this brief's standing Ravens thesis and it is now gone from the Chem wire. That branch is closed by someone else's move, not by analysis.

case.label: The board
case.body: Yahoo's Week 2 tiers put Baltimore in Tier 2 with New England, Pittsburgh, the Rams and Jacksonville. The best free defences here are New England (Tier 2) and Jacksonville (Tier 2, 37.6% owned); the Chargers and Packers are Tier 3; Detroit, Chicago and Cleveland are Tier 5, 'avoid'.

case.label: Why hold
case.body: New England is in the same tier as Baltimore, not above it. Moving a defence sideways costs a roster move and gains nothing, and this seat has already changed hands three times this month.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Baltimore finishing outside the top twelve defensive scores in Week 2. The seat then opens on Tuesday, and with the 49ers gone the first name on the list is Jacksonville or New England, whichever has the better Week 3 draw.

doNotChase.sources: Yahoo Sports Week 2 D/ST tiers · ESPN league activity log

doNotChase.name: Xavier Worthy
doNotChase.lead: 74% rostered nationally, free here, and a structural mismatch rather than a bargain. Carried from this morning and not re-researched tonight.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: Sharp Football Analysis on Week 1: Patrick Mahomes averaged 1.1 air yards per completion, the lowest in the league. A deep threat on a checkdown offence has neither the opportunity nor the vacated role that STRATEGY section 4 ranks above an ownership anomaly.

case.label: The branch that is closed
case.body: Rashee Rice is entirely off Kansas City's Week 2 injury report, confirmed again tonight by NBC, so the 'Worthy inherits the targets' branch cannot fire this week.

case.label: Stated as carried, not re-derived
case.body: No new Kansas City receiver reporting was pulled this run. The ownership and projection figures come from tonight's snapshot; the finding is this morning's. Saying so is the difference between a hold and an assumption.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Kansas City's air-yards profile normalising across two weeks, or Rice missing time.

doNotChase.sources: Sharp Football Analysis · NBC Sports · carried from 19 September 04:40Z

settled.result: Re-derived from the 21:52 snapshot: all 14 AVIATO players against all 126 players on the other nine rosters, scored on both sides' optimal season lineups. Zero pairs gain for both teams.

cannotSee.label: Whether Zay Flowers actually plays, which is the whole Andrews card
cannotSee.body: Baltimore's own Friday report says DOUBTFUL and Sports Illustrated reported he did very little at that session. ESPN's league file has already moved him to OUT. Those are two different answers and I have taken ESPN's, because the file is what your app scores against. Sunday's inactive list at 10:30 is the only thing that settles it, and it lands after this brief was written.

cannotSee.label: Miami's quarterback is carried from this morning, not re-verified tonight
cannotSee.body: The 13:30 run established Malik Willis under centre with Tyreek Hill cut and Jaylen Waddle traded, and tonight's snapshot agrees — Waddle is on Panda Attack's bench listed at Denver and Hill sits on the wire at 5% owned and OUT. But I could not retrieve a Week 2 source naming Miami's starter tonight. Achane caught 67 passes last season; in full PPR, who is throwing is half his value.

cannotSee.label: Two tiles are dashed and the reason is different for each
cannotSee.body: Kyle Pitts has no Carolina-against-tight-ends research; Kyle Monangai has no Minnesota-against-backs research. Both are bench players and neither dash changes a decision. Everything else on the page is graded on a named, retrieved number.

cannotSee.label: Positional defence ranks barely exist in Week 2
cannotSee.body: Every grade here rests on one game of 2026 plus last season, which is why several rest on a team-level defensive tier or a single reported split rather than a positional rank. STRATEGY section 8 says weeks 1–3 are noise and that applies to the tiles as much as to the box scores. Treat the green as weaker than it looks.

cannotSee.label: Two sources disagree about your kicker and I picked one
cannotSee.body: Pro Football Network have Loop K4 this week; Sports Illustrated have him 18th on a season-long tier, off a missed Week 18 game-winner and Baltimore signing competition. I took the weekly board because the decision is weekly. If Loop misses twice, SI were right and this brief was wrong to wave them off.

cannotSee.label: Rivals' pending waiver claims are invisible
cannotSee.body: ESPN only ever returns your own. Mark Andrews is a free agent so nobody can claim him ahead of you — but any of the other nine managers can simply add him first, and nothing in this snapshot sees that coming. The 49ers D/ST went exactly that way tonight at 20:13.

cannotSee.label: Season projections are still frozen
cannotSee.body: Tonight's exhaustive Chem pair search returned the same zero as the 17 September one, and the Lamar arithmetic in your other league has returned the identical +40.6 since 17 September — days apart. That is what a preseason artifact looks like. Every trade conclusion here is priced on August's opinion until it is disproved, which is one reason the trade section is empty rather than speculative.

cannotSee.label: One of your starters plays Monday and one has already played
cannotSee.body: Josh Allen is banked at 40.8 and Isaiah Likely does not kick off until 18:15 Monday. Seven of your nine starters resolve on Sunday, so the roster table is measuring three different things in one column.

cannotSee.label: This brief does not refresh
cannotSee.body: It is as old as the 21:52 snapshot in the header. Inactive lists land about 90 minutes before kickoff and nothing here updates to reflect them. The next scheduled run is tomorrow afternoon, after every Sunday kickoff.
